title: Timeline cursor, zoom & filter interactions — working notes
content:
Context and goals:

- Problem: our current trace viewer waterfall is dense and difficult to inspect when traces contain many short-lived spans and nested fan-outs. Product asks for faster drill-down, better multi-span selection, and more discoverable filter flows for debugging latency regressions.
- Objective: propose interactions for a timeline-centric view that supports fine-grained cursor inspection, focused zoom, and on-demand multi-span comparisons while keeping the primary waterfall compact.
- Audience: SREs, infra/platform engineers, backend service owners, and solutions engineers debugging customer incidents.

Design constraints / assumptions:

- Must reuse existing span data model (id, parent_id, start_ns, duration_ns, service, operation, tags) — no schema changes for launch.
- Performance budget: timeline must render ~200 spans smoothly on mid-tier laptops (WebGL allowed for rendering).
- Accessibility: keyboard-only navigation and screen-reader labels for selected span(s).
- Mobile: not primary; interactions should degrade gracefully but not optimized for tiny screens.

Key interaction primitives (sketch-level):

1) Cursor probe (hover + focus)
- Hovering over timeline shows a vertical probe line at cursor time with a tooltip showing: absolute timestamp, nano-offset relative to trace start, and list of top 3 spans under cursor ordered by nesting depth.
- Tooltip quick actions: copy timestamp, set as zoom center, pin as named bookmark.
- Keyboard: left/right arrows move probe by configurable step (10ms/100ms/1s), shift+arrow for larger jumps. Enter pins the probe.
- Implementation note: probe is purely client-side; no new server calls when moving.

2) Focus zoom (local magnifier)
- Click-drag horizontally across the timeline to create a zoom box. Live preview shows magnified region above the timeline (peek window).
- Double-click a span to zoom to its parent scope (if any) and center on the span.
- Zoom levels: fractional (continuous) and quick-zoom presets (1s, 10s, 1m).
- When zoomed, the left gutter shows a condensed overview (mini-waterfall) with the zoom region highlighted; clicking the mini-map recenters zoom.

3) Multi-span selection and comparison
- SHIFT+click to add spans to selection, showing a comparison panel that lists selected spans side-by-side: service, op, duration, start offset, key tags (http.status, db.rows, error).
- Selection persists across zoom changes until cleared. Keyboard: Tab cycles through selected spans; Delete removes.
- Quick diffing: an inline sparkline for each selected span showing CPU/IO annotations (if available).
- CTA: "Open as analysis" creates a temp saved view (client-side) that can be exported as a permalink or attached to a support ticket.

4) Smart filters & guided queries
- Three filter modes: ad-hoc (text), guided (presets), and lens (shelf of common filters).
- Guided presets examples: ">95th latency", "DB calls > 3", "Span errors", "fan-out > 10 spans". These are editable and show example hits before applying.
- Lens: small pill UI (left of timeline) with draggable lenses for service, operation, host, and tag. Dropping a lens onto the timeline highlights spans that match and dims others.
- Text mode supports simple grammar: service:cart duration:>200ms tag:retry=true. Autocomplete shows top 50 values observed across trace.

5) Contextual collapsing & aggregation
- Provide syntactic collapsing: collapse subtrees beyond N depth into a single aggregated bar labeled "3 spans — db.*" with aggregated duration (sum, p50, p95).
- Hovering aggregated bar expands an inline list (popover) showing top contributors so you can inspect without full expansion.

6) Keyboard-first workflows
- Global shortcuts: F to focus timeline, / to open filter, Z to toggle zoom, P to pin probe.
- Arrow keys: left/right move probe; up/down jump across sibling spans.
- Action mode: press A to open action palette for selected span (open logs, replay request, copy span id).

7) Bookmarks, notes, and share links
- Pin probe or selection with a short note; pins show timestamp and note on top bar.
- Export permalink encodes current filter, zoom, and pinned spans (URL length limit addressed by shortlink service).

Edge cases and decision points:

- Long traces (10k+ spans): fall back to a sampling or aggregator rendering mode that shows aggregated bands by service, with affordances to fetch surrounding detail on demand. UX should make it clear sampling occurred.
- Clock skew and negative durations: show skew indicator and allow toggling "align by parent start" vs. "absolute ns".
- Multi-region/replicated traces: show region lane toggle to collapse/expand replicas.
- When span widths become <1px: show heatmap overlay vs per-span bar to preserve pattern visibility.

Open questions for grooming:

- Which quick-zoom presets should be default? (Propose: 250ms, 1s, 10s, full-trace)
- Should aggregator bars support different aggregation functions (sum vs. max) and which should we expose in UI?
- How should guided filters be curated — product managed or community-editable?
- Telemetry: which interactions must fire events for analytics (probe moves, zoom, selection exports, lens drops)? Need list for instrumentation.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):

- Cursor probe with tooltip and keyboard movement implemented and instrumented.
- Click-drag zoom that changes visible time window and updates mini-overview map.
- SHIFT+click multi-selection with comparison panel showing 5 core fields (service, operation, duration, start offset, error tag).
- Filter input accepting text queries with autocomplete for services and top tags.
- Export permalink for current view that resolves to same state for other users.

Non-goals for MVP:

- Full WebGL-powered rendering pipeline (can be phased in).
- Mobile-optimized interactions.
- Deep APM integrations (profiles, CPU/heap) beyond inline sparklines.

Sketch notes / rapid wireframe annotations (for design handoff):

- Canvas layout: left gutter (span tree with collapsible parents), main timeline canvas, right rail (selected span details), top mini-overview map, bottom action bar (filters, lenses, bookmarks).
- Colors: use service color tokens from design system; ensure colorblind-safe palette for 8+ services. Use lower-saturation colors for dimmed spans when filter is active.
- Tooltip: compact two-column layout, max 10 lines. Avoid overflow by truncation with ellipses and full-view link.
- Microcopy examples: tooltip CTA "Zoom here (Z)"; pin action label "Pin probe — add note".

Grooming checklist (to break into tickets):

- [ ] Probe hover + tooltip — front-end only.
- [ ] Probe keyboard movement + instrumentation.
- [ ] Click-drag zoom + mini-map highlight.
- [ ] Double-click zoom to parent.
- [ ] Shift+click multi-select + comparison panel.
- [ ] Filter input with service/tag autocomplete.
- [ ] Lens drag-and-drop prototype.
- [ ] Aggregation bar UX + hover popover.
- [ ] Permalink encoding + shortlink service integration.
- [ ] Accessibility review and keyboard tests.

Attachments / sketches to add: (TODO)
- Quick PNG wireframes for normal, zoomed, and aggregated modes.
- Sequence diagram for probe interactions and selection persistence.

Notes and follow-ups:

- Spike: measure render performance on 2-year-old MacBook Air with 200 spans and 1k spans to determine threshold for switching to aggregator mode (Evan to own).
- Research: gather top 20 filter predicates used in last 6 months from analytics to seed Guided presets (Priya to own).
- Design review scheduled: Feb 13 2025 10:00 AM PST — invite: product, eng-serving-runtime, s-reliability, devexp.

Quick links for reviewers: GH-PR: /redwood/console/compare/timeline-probe (draft), Confluence: trace-viewer-v2/interaction-specs.

Small disclaimers:
- This doc focuses on interaction ideas, not visual polish. Expect iteration after design and engineering feasibility checks.
- Keep backward compatibility with current trace URLs as a priority when implementing permalink design.

End of notes.
